ground_truth_core_content:
Introduction:
**1:** Both sections cover the recap, the transition to multimodality, and why text-only systems fail on visually-rich content, naming financial reports, medical/X-ray imaging, technical diagrams, and building sketches -- all of the expected section's named examples, plus audio logs as a complementary addition.

Limitations of Traditional Document Processing:
**1:** Both sections cover the OCR pipeline, rigid/fragile/costly framing, cascading errors, and failure-mode statistics, naming nested tables and building sketches as complex-layout examples. All substantive ideas present in the expected section are present here.

Foundations of Multimodal LLMs:
**1:** Both sections cover both architectures, all three named image encoders, the model landscape, modality extension, and the diffusion distinction, enriched with a well-anchored addition connecting video-understanding temporal-modeling research (STORM) to future document-LLM spatial-layout analysis. No expected idea is displaced.

Applying Multimodal LLMs to Images and PDFs:
**1:** Both sections cover raw bytes (including the two-image comparison demonstration), Base64, public URLs, private-data-lake URLs, object detection, and PDF-as-bytes with object detection, plus a well-anchored addition on Gemini's own production failure modes. The one gap -- processing PDFs as a Base64-encoded string -- is a single missing demonstration step within an otherwise comprehensive section.

Foundations of Multimodal RAG:
**0:** Both sections cover the generic RAG architecture, ColPali's OCR-bypassing role and bag-of-embeddings representation. However, two distinct substantive facts present in the expected section are absent here: (1) the PaliGemma-3B/SigLIP model composition and the GitHub repository reference, the same recurring gap found in every article graded this session but one; and (2) the ViDoRe benchmark and its 81.3% average nDCG@5 score -- the expected section's headline performance figure -- which is entirely absent, replaced instead by a different set of benchmark figures (financial-domain nDCG@5 gains, DocVQA scores) drawn from exploration research. The presence of alternative benchmark data does not substitute for the specific ViDoRe/81.3% fact the expected section states.

Implementing Multimodal RAG for Images, PDFs and Text:
**1:** Both sections cover the image grid, create_vector_index, the helper functions, search_multimodal, both example queries, and a closing synthesis statement about extending the unified index to video/audio that closely mirrors the expected section's own framing. The one gap -- a missing demonstration of the vector_index's keys/first-element content -- is a single minor omission.

Building Multimodal AI Agents:
**1:** Both sections cover the ways multimodal capability is added to agents, tool-wrapping, building the ReAct agent, and the kitten-color question through to the final answer, plus two well-anchored additions on robotics/autonomous-driving and edge-AI applications. As in every replicate graded so far, the expected section's Figure 23 has no counterpart, but that is a Flow matter, not a CoreContent one.

Conclusion:
**0:** Both sections frame the lesson as the close of Part 1 and recap the course arc. However, the expected section's specific claim -- that the Part 2 capstone's research agent will handle multimodal data and pass it to the writer agent -- is absent; the generated section previews Part 2 only as 'a complete, multi-agent research and writing pipeline' with no multimodal connection stated.

References:
**1:** Both sections contain a numbered list of references serving the same bibliographic purpose.
